claim: The Prometheus Node Exporter HA add-on (loganmarchione, community-distributed) requires disabling HAOS 'Protection mode' because node_exporter needs host-level access to read host CPU/memory/disk metrics from inside its container.
stance_target: Gap/awkwardness in the HAOS add-on approach to host metrics that a native agent avoids
scope_conditions: HAOS add-on ecosystem, prometheus node_exporter, 2021-2026 community thread
quoted_support: Node exporter requires host-level access (since it's running in a container) so that it can read CPU, memory, disk, etc… of the host. This is why protection mode needs to be disabled.

claim: Users confirm the official HA Prometheus integration exports only entity-related metrics, not host-related metrics, which is why a separate node_exporter add-on exists at all.
stance_target: HA lacks native host-metrics collection - the gap ha-linux-agent fills for jupiterOS hosts
quoted_support: Doesn't Home Assistant already have Prometheus integration? Yes, but the official integration only exposes entity-related metrics, not host-related metrics.

claim: The add-on was only tested on amd64 initially, with aarch64 (RPi 4) added after user request, and the Open Web UI button breaks when HA is behind a reverse proxy; SSL exposure was deliberately deferred to the user's proxy layer.
stance_target: Operational fragility of the add-on distribution path (multi-arch coverage, proxying, TLS) vs a native NixOS-packaged agent
quoted_support: Only tested on amd64 builds. ... The "Open Web UI" button doesn't work when Home Assistant is behind a reverse proxy. ... It shouldn't be my add-on's job to do that [SSL].
